note: Built around the 1940s-50s Port-au-Prince dance orchestras, above all Issa El-Saieh's La Belle Créole 78s, whose labels and discography mark each side 'Meringue' (with Guy Durosier, Wébert Sicot and Bebo Valdés's Haitian sessions), and around the salon méringue for piano: Fabre Duroseau's 1952 Folkways recordings and Ludovic Lamothe playing his own 'Nibo' for Lomax in 1937. Péligre is a carnival méringue of 1955. The Lomax tracks were recorded 1936-37 and first issued in 2009; the Destiné track is from 1952-62 and first issued in 2015. Saintonge's Élégie-Méringue and Casséus's Méringue Frangeul are modern recordings of art pieces. Choucoune ('Ti zwazo', 1893) is the best-known méringue of all.

size.basis: A judgement, not a count. What is on record: Issa El-Saieh's La Belle Créole label alone issued about 35 sides marked (Meringue) between 1947 and 1956 (French Wikipedia discography), alongside the other Port-au-Prince dance orchestras of the 1940s-50s; Folkways (Haitian Piano, 1952; Calypso and Meringues, 1953) and Remington (Emy de Pradines, Original Meringues, 1953) LPs; Seeco and French 78s of Haitian méringues; the 1936-37 Lomax field recordings; reissue compilations (Corason 1993, Frémeaux 2015, Ostinato 2016 still uses the label for 1960-1981 records); and a small art-music shelf of recorded piano and guitar méringues (Duroseau, Saintonge, Casséus). After the mid-1950s most Haitian dance records are filed as kompa rather than méringue, which caps the range. An insider's essential list is about 40 recordings, most of them 1937-1960 orchestra sides and salon piano pieces.
